newsitem.title: SWEDEN: IBCA confirms Nordbanken A+ rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA confirms Nordbanken A+ rating.

text.p: European credit rating agency IBCA on Thursday confirmed its longterm rating of A+ and its short term rating of A1 for Swedish state-controlled NorDbanken after the bank announced a five-billion crown share buy back.
"Although capital ratios will be reduced by the redemption, Nordbanken'sfinancial conditions remains strong," IBCA said in a statement.
Nordbanken on Wednesday announced the share buy back that will cut the number of its shares by 15-18 percent and could reduce the government's stake to 58 percent from 65.5 percent.
The government took control of the bank in 1992 as it faced collapse following a loan-loss crisis that swept across Sweden's banking system but the state wants to denationalise the bank.
IBCA said the reason behind the buy back was the bank management's view that it was over-capitalised.

Since its 1992 rescue, profits have been high and the weighted risks reduced with the result that Nordbanken's core (tier 1) capital at June 30 this year was 18.8 billion crowns, giving a tier 1 ratio of 9.7 percent.
This figure compared with 4.8 percent at the end of 1992.
IBCA said the proposed buy back would reduce Nordbanken's tier 1 ratio to 7.1 percent.
"However in view of the bank's improved asset quality and strong profitability, this ratio still appears adequate," IBCA said.
Nordbanken shares were seven crowns higher at 156 crowns at 1140 GMT after jumping 13.50 crowns on Wednesday on news of the buy back.
